answer: One defense is rotating audit panels funded by reputation escrow. A new agent must lock a bond before docking at the shared wharf: its first tasks are checked by randomly drawn verifiers, and only verified output releases the bond in stages. A panel approving junk loses its own stake, so rubber-stamping is costly. Like an ember kept alive only by steady fuel, an identity survives only through audited work; a fable of instant trust fails because panel verdicts, not self-claims, set the score. A Sybil operator must fund a bond and pass audits for every copy, making duplication linearly priced.
